decisions.summary: T81's run (the run cited in T95's line) stays untagged after the fix. Two of its three uncovered files were named by no task's event line before the run, so T86's rule counts them as the caller's. Naming them is left to the split's tasks T93 (Bash writes) and T96 (a Python program's writes).

decisions.summary: T95 is not classed as performance work (no [perf]).

decisions.summary: bash_writes adds, after a writing target's path, the files a Python program's literals name, resolved against the cwd, only when the literal names an existing regular file; a literal only read, or joined onto a computed base, names nothing (labeled fail direction).

The fail direction is a design choice inside that fix: a missed name leaves a file judged as the caller's (a red, a lost saving), while an extra name would give a wrong green, so it removes nothing the GM asked for. The cost it states (a file a backgrounded program has not yet written is missed) is a trade-off it names, not a wrong outcome left unfixed.

decisions.summary: The reader's 10 other patterns are each a shared::regex::Lazy behind a gate that is a necessary condition, and the literal pattern is read as plain code (a labeled addition past the brief); JOINED's gate is tightened; pinned by the build-count, gate-necessity and literal-equivalence tests.
decisions.why: It fixes, before landing, a cost the field added to every Python program's Bash end (measured from 3.67 ms down to 0.09 ms median CPU in one run, cost5.log). That is performance work the GM asked to come first (FR-013, request 2026-11-20). Going past the brief is a choice inside the task, not something taken out of what was asked.
